bibliography.abstract: This study proposes GITSR, a Graph Interaction Transformer-based Scene Representation framework for multi-vehicle collaborative decision-making. In mixed traffic environments where connected automated vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) coexist, effective scene understanding and interaction modeling are essential for safe and efficient decision-making. GITSR first extracts driving environment features under an intelligent connected vehicle setting. Then, an agent-centric dynamic occupancy grid is encoded by a Transformer module to obtain local scene representations. Meanwhile, vehicle motion information is modeled as graph structures, and spatial interaction features among traffic participants are extracted using a Graph Neural Network (GNN). Finally, the collaborative decision-making process is formulated as a Markov Decision Process, and driving actions are generated through reinforcement learning algorithms. The proposed framework is validated in a challenging highway off-ramp scenario. Simulation results show that GITSR effectively captures scene representations and spatial interaction information, outperforming baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics.
bibliography.title: GITSR: graph interaction transformer-based scene representation for multi-vehicle collaborative decision-making

en.caveats: Evaluation is limited to simulated highway off-ramp scenarios and may not reflect performance in real-world urban street networks.
en.what: The authors developed GITSR, a framework for multi-vehicle collaborative decision-making in mixed traffic consisting of connected automated vehicles and human-driven vehicles. The method combines a Transformer module to encode local scenes from agent-centric dynamic occupancy grids with a Graph Neural Network to extract spatial interactions from vehicle motion graphs. When paired with reinforcement learning in a Markov Decision Process formulation, the system outperformed baseline decision-making methods in a simulated highway off-ramp environment.
en.why: It improves dynamic scene representation and spatial interaction modeling for autonomous driving fleets, allowing connected automated vehicles to navigate complex highway merge and off-ramp bottlenecks more effectively alongside human drivers.
